end.parentNote: Gauri practised finding partners that make 10 using fingers, counting, and beads. They correctly used 7 and 3 and found that 8 needs 2; Asha also introduced 6 and 4 and other pairs. Gauri first mixed up the idea by thinking only 5 and 5 makes 10, and this was not corrected by the last response. At home, make pairs with 10 small objects and ask, “If I move some to the other group, how many are left?”
